clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11445 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
clauses.reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11445 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

research_rationale:
EO 11445 (1969-01-13, 34 FR 545) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11445.txt, 34 FR 545, PDF pages 9-10) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. savings.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.
